method: A Permissions-Policy header is a structured-field dictionary: comma-separated members of the form feature=allowlist. The allowlist may be the token * for every origin, the token self, an empty inner list () that blocks the feature, or a parenthesized list in which the keywords stay bare and every origin is a quoted string, as in geolocation=(self "https://maps.example.com"). * and () may only stand alone, while self and src may be combined with origins; src names an iframe's own URL, so it matches nothing in a response header and the page warns when it is used. A source is a scheme-source (https:) or a host-source of scheme, host and optional port, with an optional wildcard label (https://*.example.com) or wildcard port (https://example.com:*). The page lowercases the scheme and host, drops port 443 for https and 80 for http, drops a trailing slash, and refuses a path, query, fragment or credentials instead of leaving the browser to ignore the member. Duplicate member names are refused because a dictionary with a repeated key is invalid, and a repeated origin is kept once with a warning. Features omitted from the header keep their default allowlist, so the page never invents a permissive entry for them. A name outside the built-in list of standardized features is still emitted, with a warning, because browsers ignore names they do not implement and the list changes over time. Per-directive report-to endpoints are not modelled. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
